transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well. I guess I've been having a hard time lately with my work. I'm an artist, and... I was making a memorial piece for my aunt recently. 

And... I don't know, I just kept getting these really awful thoughts while I was working on it. They were just... unwanted. Like I was going to dishonor her somehow. It sounds weird to say out loud, but... I kept feeling like if I made one wrong photo placement, or just picked the wrong color... it would mean I didn't love her enough. 

I usually get regular creative doubts, you know, but this was different. I couldn't just brush these thoughts off like I normally would. So... yeah. That's why I decided to come in.
Did you feel the need to do anything specific to make these awful thoughts go away?

Um... yeah. I guess so. 

I just... I'd end up rereading the label text. A lot. And, um, just sort of... nudging the same objects around on the table. Or checking the layout photos over and over again. 

I just had to keep doing it until it felt... settled, I guess. It's embarrassing to talk about, because part of me knows it's already fine. But I just... I end up losing so much studio time over it.
Do you find yourself doing these repetitive behaviors, like rereading or rearranging, when you're not working on your art?
Um... no, not really. It's mostly just... just when I'm working on my pieces. I don't really notice it much otherwise. Just... mostly in the studio.
Do you feel like these awful thoughts about dishonoring your aunt are coming from yourself, or do they feel like they're coming from outside of yourself?

Um... I'm not really sure what you mean. They're... they're just my thoughts. Just in my head. 

I guess it's just my own brain doing it. It's not... coming from anywhere else.
Do these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt feel like they're a part of you, or do they feel alien or inconsistent with how you really think and feel?

Um... I don't really know. I haven't... I haven't really thought about it like that. 

They just sort of happen. I don't really know if they feel alien or... whatever. I just... I just worry about it. That's all.
Have these thoughts or behaviors been affecting your daily life outside of your studio in any significant way?

Um... I mean, I'm still getting most of my work done. So it's mostly fine. 

It's just... because of the extra time I lose when I'm in the studio, it kind of pushes other things back. Like... I ended up missing a grant deadline recently. And... um... I had to back out of a gallery talk I actually really wanted to do. I just didn't have the time. 

So... yeah, I guess it affects things a little. But that's about it.
Do you feel like these thoughts and behaviors are causing you significant distress?

Um... I mean... it's stressful, I guess. 

I don't know if I'd call it significant. It's just... frustrating. That's all.
Do you feel like these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt are in line with your own values and beliefs?

Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't... I don't really look at it like that. 

I just... I care about her, so I don't want to do anything wrong. I don't really know about... values and all that. It's just what goes through my head.
Would you say that these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt come into your mind against your will?

Um... yeah, I guess so. 

I don't really want to think about it. It's just... when I was working on her memorial piece, I kept getting these awful thoughts. Like... if I put a photo in the wrong place, or picked the wrong color, it meant I was dishonoring her. Or that I didn't love her enough. 

They just kind of... pop up. And I can't really brush them off like regular doubts. They just stay there.
Do you feel like these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt are something you would normally think, or are they somehow foreign to your own way of thinking?

Um... I'm not really sure. I mean... they're in my head, so I guess they're my thoughts. 

I don't really know what you mean by foreign. It's just... what's been happening lately. I haven't really thought about it beyond that.
Have you ever felt the need to perform these repetitive behaviors, like rereading or rearranging, in situations unrelated to your art or your aunt's memorial piece?

Um... I guess so. Sometimes. 

Like, if I'm setting up for a show... I'll end up rereading the gallery labels a bunch of times. Or I'll keep nudging the same objects on the display table... checking the layout photos over and over. 

I just keep doing it until it feels... settled, I guess. Even when part of me knows it's already fine. I just end up wasting my studio time doing it.
Do you ever feel the need to perform these repetitive behaviors when you're not thinking about your aunt or working on your art?
Um... no, not really. It's mostly just... with my art. Or the things for my aunt. I don't really notice it other times.
When you're rereading the labels or rearranging objects, are you trying to make sure everything is perfect or are you trying to stop the unwanted thoughts from coming into your mind?

Um... I don't know if it's about the thoughts. It's more just... I have to make it feel right. 

Like I said, I just end up rereading the text on the labels, or... nudging the objects around on the table. Checking the photos over and over. I just keep doing it until it feels... settled. Even though I know it's fine. I just... I end up wasting my studio time on it.
Do you ever have these unwanted, awful thoughts when you're not working on your art or thinking about your aunt?

Um... no. Not really. It's... it's just when I'm working on her memorial piece. 

That's actually why I came in. I just... I kept getting these awful thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. Like, if I chose the wrong color, or put a photo in the wrong place... it meant I didn't love her enough. 

It's not like normal creative doubts. I just... I can't brush them off. But it's really just about her piece.
When you're rereading the labels or rearranging objects, are you trying to prevent something bad from happening?

Um... no, not really preventing anything. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it's just... I end up checking the layout photos over and over, or rereading the text. Just nudging the same objects on the table. 

I just have to do it until it feels settled. Part of me knows it's already fine, but... I just keep losing my studio time doing it.
Do you feel like these thoughts about dishonoring your aunt are something that you would normally think, or do they feel out of character for you?

Um... yeah, they're not normal for me. They're definitely out of character. 

Like I was saying before... they're just really unwanted. Usually, I just have normal creative doubts when I work. But these are... they're awful, and I can't just brush them off like I normally would. The idea that just... one wrong photo placement or a bad color choice means I didn't love her enough, or that I'm going to dishonor her... I don't normally think like that. It's just... yeah. Not normal for me.
Are you doing these repetitive behaviors, like rereading or rearranging, to try to reduce your anxiety about dishonoring your aunt?

Um... I guess so. Yeah. 

It's just... like I said, I end up rereading the text, or... checking the layout photos again and again. Or just... nudging the objects on the table. 

I just... I do it until the feeling goes away. Until it feels settled. Even though I know it's fine, I just... I keep doing it, and then my studio time is gone. But yeah, it's... I guess it's to make that feeling stop.
Are you doing these repetitive behaviors to try to prevent something bad from happening to your aunt's memory or to you?

I... no, I don't think it's about preventing anything bad. 

Like I just said, it's... I just end up rereading the text and checking the layout photos over and over. Or nudging the same things on the table. I just do it until it feels settled. Even though part of me knows it's already fine... I just keep losing my studio time doing it.
Would you say that these thoughts and behaviors are causing you a lot of distress?
Um... I guess so. It's... it's bothersome. I don't know if I'd say a lot, but... it's definitely frustrating.
Would you say that these thoughts and behaviors are causing you significant distress, to the point where it's affecting your overall well-being?

I... well, I'm still getting most of my work done. It's not like I've stopped working. But... I guess it is getting in the way a little. 

Just because of the extra time I lose in the studio... it already cost me a grant deadline. And... I ended up backing out of a gallery talk I had actually wanted to do. So... yeah. I suppose it is affecting things.
